title: He solved a physics puzzle in 1989. In 2026, it won him a first no Indian-origin scientist had ever had.
sources: Global Indian, 2026 - Jainendra Jain, Indian-origin recipient of Wolf Prize in Physics
American Bazaar, 2026 - Jainendra K. Jain becomes first Indian-origin scientist to win Wolf Prize in Physics
caption:
In 1989, a young physicist solved a puzzle nobody else could explain. In 2026, that work made him the first Indian-origin scientist to win the Wolf Prize in Physics.

Jainendra Jain, born in Sambhar, Rajasthan, received the prize on June 18, 2026 in Jerusalem, honored for a 1989 discovery made at Yale: 'composite fermions,' a theory explaining why electrons behave in precise fractional patterns under strong magnetic fields - the fractional quantum Hall effect. The patterns are now called 'Jain sequences,' and the work underlies today's research into quantum computing.

He also directs a physics institute in Mumbai - a theory built abroad, still finding its way back to build something at home.
